posts.quote:
Julio Cesar Chavez x KRONK 🇲🇽

Following the first loss of his career against Frankie Randall, Mexican hero Julio Cesar Chavez teamed up with legendary realkronkgym trainer Emanuel Steward for the rematch.

Chavez trained from deep in the heart of Mexico, travelling north stopping at various cities along the way to let the fans see him.

Hundreds, and at times thousands, would pack in to watch him spar and he was frequently mobbed in the streets.

He carried the pressure of a nation heading into the Randall rematch, with Mexico’s President even calling him during training camp.

Steward knew that only small adjustments would be necessary for Chavez to have his revenge. He brought in unbeaten lightweight Michael “Cold Blood” Clark to mimic Randall’s style in camp.

The Hall of Fame duo went 3-0 while working together. First, Chavez got his revenge against Randall in their immediate rematch. Wins against Meldrick Taylor and Tony Lopez then followed.

Take a rare look inside their training camp for the Randall rematch where Steward guided one of Mexico’s true greats.

posts.name: Willy Hutchinson
posts.quote:
From the age of 9, when I first stepped into a boxing gym, to becoming Amateur World Champion at 18, and now winning the WBC World Championship at just 28. It’s honestly unbelievable.

The ups and downs, the highs and lows, the sacrifices and everything in between. I can genuinely say I’m incredibly grateful for the journey so far. 

A massive thank you to everyone who sent their best wishes before the fight and to the thousands of people who have sent messages of congratulations since. I’ve read so many of them, and I appreciate every single one of you. Your support means more than you know. 

Two chapters of the book are now complete. Amateur World Champion. Professional WBC World Champion.

But the story is far from finished…

Now it’s time to push on and unify the division.

#worldchampion #wbc #boxing #lifeisgood #thefuture
